metadata.note: Illinois Central's Chicago-New Orleans flagship trains, the historical predecessors of Amtrak's City of New Orleans (which kept the name). Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; any place where the historical routing differed is described in the segment notes and reflected in the geometry. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones (train introductions, renamings, mergers, discontinuation dates); headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables. EXPANDED 2026-08-18: added the pre-1911 history that was previously missing entirely -- the original 1856 Chicago-Cairo land-grant main line (a real subset of the same GTFS-derived geometry, sliced at Cairo, IL), and the 1877-1911 Chicago-St.Louis-New Orleans general-service era after the New Orleans, Jackson & Great Northern and Mississippi Central mergers created the first continuous Chicago-New Orleans route, predating the Panama Limited by 34 years.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (City of New Orleans, Panama Limited), american-rails.com
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.line: Illinois Central: Chicago – Cairo (original main line)
properties.speed_source: estimated: 1850s-70s steam-era mixed local/through service; unsourced

segments.note: The Illinois Central was chartered Feb 10 1851 as the first federal land-grant railroad in U.S. history; construction began Dec 1851, and the Chicago-Cairo line (with its companion Centralia-Galena branch) opened complete in 1856, at 700+ miles briefly the longest railroad in the world. This was the whole of the IC before it reached New Orleans -- see the Chicago-New Orleans feature below for the 1877 through connection. Frequency estimated, unsourced

properties.company: Chicago, St. Louis and New Orleans Railroad / Illinois Central Railroad
properties.line: Chicago, St. Louis and New Orleans: Chicago – New Orleans (general service)

segments.note: The Illinois Central acquired the New Orleans, Jackson & Great Northern (Mar 1877) and the Mississippi Central (Aug 1877), merging them Nov 7 1877 into the Chicago, St. Louis and New Orleans Railroad -- the first continuous Chicago-New Orleans line, 548 miles of new trackage south of Cairo. IC leased the CStL&NO in 1882 (a 400-year lease) and converted its broad gauge to standard in a single 24-hour operation on Jul 29 1881. General/named service predates the 1911 Panama Limited; frequency estimated, unsourced

properties.line: Illinois Central: City of New Orleans
properties.speed_source: estimated/blended across the line's history; unsourced

segments.note: Introduced Apr 27 1947 as an all-coach daytime companion to the overnight Panama Limited, covering the 921-mile route in 15h55m - the longest daytime schedule in the United States - with EMD E7s and new lightweight Pullman coaches. Amtrak took over May 1 1971 and still runs the name today - see amtrak.geojson. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
